newsitem.title: FRANCE: Serbia opposition to end street demos if law voted.
newsitem.headline: Serbia opposition to end street demos if law voted.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders said on Thursday they would end street protests against President Slobodan Milosevic if parliament next Tuesday approved a bill reinstating their municipal election victories in 14 cities.

"We will stop the demonstrations and will give a chance to dialogue" if parliament approves the bill, Vuk Draskovic, a leader of the democratic Zajedno coalition, told reporters after meeting French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
But the three Zajedno (Together) leaders remained cautious about the hardline Socialist president's sudden decision to reinstate opposition election victories after 11 weeks of street protests.
"I don't think this is the end," said Vesna Pesic.
"We must be very , very careful. We had very bad experiences of Mr Milosevic in the past," Draskovic said.

In a policy switch, France invited Draskovic, Pesic and Zoran Djindjic, the three Zajedno leaders, on a brief visit to Paris after Serbian police used violence against peaceful demonstrators earlier this week, saying the invitation amounted to recognition of the coalition.
Foreign Minister Herve de Charette hailed the maturity of the coalition and, in a warm show of support, was photographed in a handshake with the three leaders.
Draskovic said all three opposition leaders agreed to give a chance to talks on other issues of democratic reform.

De Charette said Serbia's problems should be resolved by recognition of the election results, dialogue between the government and the opposition, democratic elections as planned by the end of this year and free access to the media.
"France is available to give its full support to the implementation of these four provisions. I want to believe that this is the process Mr Milosevic wants to carry out," he said.
He said France would contact other European Union governments to work out a common way of backing moves towards democracy in Serbia.
Draskovic said that Milosevic's decision was "Good. What is not good is the fact that Mr Milosevic did this after 80 days of peaceful demonstrations all over Serbia" , he said.
He added that if Milosevic failed to carry through democratic reforms "it would be very easy for us to have 100,000 people on the streets of Serbia overnight".
